findings.body:
Adding any *unrelated* label re-reds a gate that already passed. The workflow subscribes to `labeled` for every label (`self-review.yml:50`), so after a `ready` review goes green, a bot `dependencies` bump fires a new run on the **same head SHA**: `scope` emits `[]` (lines 104–114), this check fails, and the PR is re-blocked with the message "apply the 'ready' label" — which is wrong, the label *is* applied. The comment's "only path is a missing `ready` label" is also false when every provider secret is unset.

It fails safe (still blocks), so this is semantics, not a hole. Suggest having `scope` emit a reason output (`no-ready-label` / `label-present-event-not-ready` / `no-secrets`), branching the error text here, and documenting in TRIGGER_MODES.md technique 3 that any non-`ready` label re-reds a passed gate — with the unblock being remove+re-add `ready`, or re-running the last green gate run (cheaper than a re-review). This is exactly the accident TRIGGER_MODES.md § "webhook-vs-gate" promises users don't need to worry about.

This example's `gate-decision` job doesn't exist anywhere in the recipe: technique 2 names its decision job `gate` (line 80, consumed as `needs.gate.outputs.matrix` at line 111). A consumer assembling the full recipe from this doc pastes two jobs keyed `gate:` — a duplicate YAML key that fails to parse — and the rename is never stated.

```suggestion
    needs: [gate-decision, review]    # = technique 2's decision job ('gate'), renamed here because THIS job takes the 'gate' name
```

This rename leaves `README.md:291` quoting the old section title: "docs/TRIGGER_MODES.md § 'Recipe: run once when labelled `ready`, and show Skipped (not green)'". The href carries no anchor fragment, so nothing 404s, but the quoted § name no longer exists for readers following the README. Update that link text in this PR (AGENTS.md Rule #7 — docs stay in sync).

summary:
Solid, well-reasoned CI fix. The core diagnosis is correct and I verified it against the workflow: GitHub branch protection treats a *Skipped* required check as passing, so a stable-named `gate` job with `if: always()` that *fails* is the right shape, and the `SCOPE_RESULT` → `MATRIX` → `REVIEW_RESULT` check ordering is fail-safe (a scope crash blocks, a cancelled review blocks, skipped legs can't slip through). All `${{ }}` expressions enter the script through `env:` mapping — no shell-injection surface — and the job inherits the workflow-level `permissions:` block, adds no third-party actions, and needs no checkout.

One warning: the workflow subscribes to `labeled` for *any* label and `scope` emits `[]` for unrelated labels, so once a gate has gone green after a `ready` review, adding an unrelated label (e.g. a bot `dependencies` bump) re-fires the workflow on the same head SHA and reds the gate again — re-blocking a fully-reviewed PR, with an error message that tells the maintainer to apply a label that is already applied. It fails safe, so it's a messaging/semantics fix, not a security hole. Two info-level doc nits round it out.
